summary: Correction to evt-20260811-080207-c3b2be-worker-status-authority-audit: canonical hardening pr_check DOES consume worker status by explicitly rejecting STOPPED workers. Therefore accepting DONE as a mere additional valid enum value without semantic normalization would weaken ownership: a DONE worker with a still-live claim/resource lease would no longer hit the STOPPED guard. Any compatibility repair must normalize lifecycle aliases before authority use (DONE -> STOPPED, CLAIMING -> WORKING) or make the authority guard alias-aware. Claim/resource leases remain necessary but are not the only worker-lifecycle authority fence. The earlier event's narrower statement that worker status is validation-only is superseded by this correction.
evidence: tools/swarm/swarmctl_hardening_base.py pr_check loads the worker record and raises 'worker is STOPPED' when worker.status == STOPPED before matching the authoritative claim.
tools/swarm/swarmctl.py validates the worker status vocabulary, while pr_check in the hardening engine provides the STOPPED authority semantic.
Observed compatibility aliases still map naturally as CLAIMING -> WORKING and DONE -> STOPPED; the safe repair must preserve those semantics rather than just widening WORKER_STATUSES.

metadata.safeRepairShape: Centralize canonical worker-status normalization and use the normalized value in both validation and authority checks; keep unknown values rejected.
